entry: American rapper, songwriter, record producer and record executive. Known for his rap flow and conscious rap, which includes political criticism and social commentary, he is often credited with popularizing [[Hip-hop|hip-hop]] in Middle America. His album *The Eminem Show* (2002) was the best-selling album worldwide in 2002. He is the best-selling rapper, with estimated sales of over 220 million records, and has 11 number-one albums on the Billboard 200. He was inducted into the [[Rock and Roll Hall of Fame]] in his first year of eligibility.

Algerian religious and military leader. As an Islamic scholar and Sufi, he led a struggle against the French colonial invasion of [[Algiers]] from 1831 to 1847, assembling a coalition of Algerian tribes that resisted one of the most powerful armies in Europe for 17 years. He was appointed emir in 1832. His treatment of prisoners and civilians has often been cited as an early example of humanitarian conduct in warfare, particularly by his Christian opponents. After his surrender in 1847 he was held in [[France]] for almost five years before being released by [[Napoleon III]] and taken to [[Bursa]]. He settled in [[Damascus]] in 1855, and in 1860 his intervention halted the massacre of the Christian community there, earning him honors and awards from several countries. In Damascus he wrote his major work, *Kitab al-Mawaqif* (the "Book of Halts").

Flag carrier airline of the [[United Arab Emirates]], based in Dubai. Founded in 1985 with backing from Dubai's royal family, it is the world's largest long-haul airline and the largest in the [[Middle East]], operating more than 3,600 flights per week from its hub at [[Dubai International Airport]]. As of January 2026 it was the world's largest [[Airbus A380]] operator, with 116 aircraft in service, and the largest [[Boeing 777]] operator, with 133.

Anarchist revolutionary, political activist and writer. Born in Kaunas, then in the [[Russian Empire]], she immigrated to the United States in 1885 and was drawn to [[Anarchism|anarchism]] after the Haymarket affair in [[Chicago]]. With Alexander Berkman she planned to [[Assassination|assassinate]] Henry Clay Frick in 1892; the attempt failed. Imprisoned several times, including for "inciting to riot" and for distributing information about [[Birth control|birth control]], she founded the journal *Mother Earth* in 1906. Deported to Russia in 1919, she denounced the [[Soviet Union]] for its violent repression of independent voices. After the outbreak of the [[Spanish Civil War]] she went to Spain to support the anarchist revolution, and she died in [[Toronto]]. Admirers called her a freethinking "rebel woman," while detractors denounced her as an advocate of politically motivated murder and violent revolution.

American actress and film producer. She won two [[Academy Awards]] for Best Actress, for *La La Land* (2016) and *Poor Things* (2023). She gained wider recognition as Gwen Stacy in the [[Spider-Man]] films (2012–2014) and was the world's highest-paid actress in 2017. With her husband, Dave McCary, she founded the production company Fruit Tree in 2020.

English actress and screenwriter. She won two [[Academy Awards]]: Best Actress for *Howards End* (1992) and Best Adapted Screenplay for *Sense and Sensibility* (1995), which she wrote, making her the only person to win Oscars for both acting and writing. She was made a dame by [[Elizabeth II|Queen Elizabeth II]] in 2018 for her contributions to drama.

English actress. She first gained fame as Hermione Granger in the [[Harry Potter (film series)|Harry Potter]] films and later starred in *The Perks of Being a Wallflower* (2012) and *Little Women* (2019). She graduated from [[Brown University]] in 2014 with a bachelor's degree in English literature. That year she was appointed a UN Women Goodwill Ambassador and helped launch the HeForShe campaign for [[Gender equality|gender equality]].

French politician, president of France since 2017. Elected in 2017 with 66% of the second-round vote, defeating [[Marine Le Pen]], he became the youngest president in French history. Protests against his reforms culminated in the [[Yellow vests protests|yellow vests protests]] of 2018–2020. He led France's response to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]] from 2020. Re-elected in 2022, he joined the international condemnation of the Russian invasion of [[Ukraine]].

British suffragette and political activist. Born in the Moss Side district of [[Manchester]], she founded the all-women Women's Social and Political Union (WSPU) in 1903, dedicated to "deeds, not words." Under her leadership the group turned to physical confrontations and eventually to bombings and arson, and Pankhurst and her daughters were repeatedly imprisoned, often after hunger strikes. During the [[World War I|First World War]] she halted militancy and organized a procession to illustrate women's contribution to the war effort. The Representation of the People Act 1918 granted votes to women over 30. Though widely criticized for her militant tactics, she is recognized as a crucial element in achieving [[Women's suffrage|women's suffrage]] in the United Kingdom. She later joined the [[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservative Party]].

African American victim of lynching in [[Mississippi]]. Born and raised in [[Chicago]], Till was visiting relatives in 1955 when he was accused of flirting with, touching or whistling at a white woman, and was then abducted, beaten and shot by two men. His mother insisted on an open-casket funeral, and published photographs of his body drew national attention. An all-white jury acquitted the two men, who in a 1956 Look magazine interview confessed to the killing. Till became an icon of the [[Civil rights movement|civil rights movement]].

American football running back. He played 15 seasons in the [[National Football League|NFL]], 13 of them with the [[Dallas Cowboys]]. He holds the league's career records for rushing yards, with 18,355, and rushing touchdowns, with 164. He won three [[Super Bowl|Super Bowls]] with the Cowboys in the 1990s and was inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 2010.

German mathematician who made important contributions to abstract algebra and mathematical physics. She proved Noether's first and second theorems, which explain the connection between symmetry and conservation laws and play a fundamental role in mathematical physics. Born to a Jewish family in Erlangen, she worked without pay for seven years after her doctorate in 1907, as women were largely excluded from academic posts. In 1915 [[David Hilbert]] and Felix Klein invited her to the [[University of Göttingen]], where she developed theories of rings, fields and algebras. Her 1921 paper on ideals in commutative rings made elegant use of the ascending chain condition, and objects satisfying it are called Noetherian. In 1933 Germany's Nazi government dismissed Jews from university positions, and she moved to the United States, teaching at Bryn Mawr College in Pennsylvania. [[Albert Einstein]] and others described her as the most important woman in the history of mathematics.

Genre of rock music combining hardcore punk with emotional, often confessional lyrics. It emerged from the mid-1980s Washington, D.C., hardcore scene, reached mainstream audiences in the early 2000s and remained popular into the mid-to-late 2000s through bands such as [[Fall Out Boy]] and [[My Chemical Romance]]. Purported links to depression and [[Self-harm|self-harm]] fueled a backlash, and some bands rejected the label.

Pictogram, logogram or ideogram embedded in text and used in electronic messages. Its primary function is to supply emotional cues missing from typed conversation. The first emoji sets were created by Japanese companies in the late 1980s and 1990s, and emoji became popular worldwide in the 2010s after [[Unicode]] began encoding them. In 2015 Oxford Dictionaries named the face with tears of joy emoji its word of the year.

Ability to perceive another person's perspective and respond to their experience. Empathy is a broad term that can be divided into cognitive, emotional (affective), somatic and spiritual empathy. Research covers its development, [[Neuroscience|neuroscience]] and genetics, cross-species empathy, and impairment, and some researchers quantify it with questionnaires. The basic capacity to recognize emotions in others may be innate and unconscious, whereas imagining oneself as another person is more sophisticated. Empathy exists on a spectrum, and research supports interventions that improve it. The English word derives from the [[Ancient Greek]] *empatheia* ("physical affection or passion").

Founder and first emperor of the [[Han dynasty]] (r. 202–195 BC). Personal name Liu Bang. Born into a peasant family, he entered the [[Qin dynasty]] bureaucracy as a minor law enforcement officer, then became a rebel leader after the death of [[Qin Shi Huang]]. He forced the surrender of the Qin ruler Ziying in 206 BC. After Xiang Yu divided the former Qin Empire, Liu was forced to accept the poor, remote region of Bashu, present-day Sichuan and Chongqing; he later won the Battle of Gaixia in 202 BC and established the Han dynasty. He reduced taxes and corvée labor, promoted [[Confucianism]], and suppressed revolts by vassal rulers outside his clan. He initiated *heqin*, a system of [[Arranged marriage|arranged marriages]] with the [[Xiongnu]] to keep peace after the Han defeat at the Battle of Baideng in 200 BC.

Emperor of Japan (r. 1867–1912). Personal name Mutsuhito. His reign saw Japan transform from a feudal state under the [[Tokugawa shogunate]] into a major imperial power. His accession triggered the [[Boshin War]], in which [[Samurai|samurai]] defeated the shogunate and restored power in his name. The [[Meiji Restoration]] proclaimed the [[Empire of Japan]] in 1868, beginning the Meiji era. Documents of his reign include the Meiji Constitution of 1889 and the Imperial Rescript on Education of 1890. Military victories over China in the [[First Sino-Japanese War]] and over Russia in the [[Russo-Japanese War]] followed, and Taiwan and Korea were annexed in 1895 and 1910, respectively.

Second emperor of the [[Tang dynasty]] of China (r. 626–649). Personal name Li Shimin. He is traditionally regarded as a co-founder of the dynasty for encouraging his father to rebel against the [[Sui dynasty]] in 617. His Reign of Zhenguan is considered a golden age, and his reign became the model by which later emperors were measured. He asked officials to be loyal to policies rather than people, to eliminate [[Corruption|corruption]]. In 630 his general Li Jing defeated the Eastern Turks, and Taizong took the title Khan of Heaven. Tang armies annexed Karakhoja in 640, Karasahr in 644 and Kucha in 648. The empire covered most territory once held by the [[Han dynasty]], as well as parts of modern-day Korea, Vietnam, Russia, Mongolia, Xinjiang and Central Asia.

Founding emperor of the [[Song dynasty]] of China (r. 960–976). Personal name Zhao Kuangyin. A distinguished general of the Later Zhou dynasty, he came to power after staging a [[Coup d'état|coup]] and forcing the last Later Zhou ruler to abdicate. He conquered Southern Tang, Later Shu, Southern Han and Jingnan, reunifying most of China proper. To strengthen his control he reduced the power of military generals and relied on civilian officials. He was succeeded by his younger brother, Zhao Kuangyi (Emperor Taizong).

Founding emperor of the [[Sui dynasty]] of China (r. 581–604). Personal name Yang Jian. As a Buddhist he encouraged the spread of [[Buddhism]] through the state. After seizing power as regent in 580, he took the throne, and in 589 he reunified China proper, ending nearly three centuries of political fragmentation. His reign began the [[Grand Canal (China)|Grand Canal]], which later facilitated the integration of northern and southern China. It was said that enough food was stored for 50 years. By the end of his reign the [[Göktürks]] had split into eastern and western khaganates, the eastern one nominally submissive to Sui.

Seventh emperor of the [[Han dynasty]] of China (r. 141–87 BC). Personal name Liu Che. His 54-year reign was not surpassed until that of the [[Kangxi Emperor]], and it brought the greatest territorial expansion of the Han dynasty, with borders from the Fergana Valley to northern Korea and northern Vietnam. He repelled the [[Xiongnu]] and sent [[Zhang Qian]] into the Western Regions in 139 BC, leading to diplomatic missions to [[Central Asia]]. He adopted [[Confucianism]] as the state philosophy and started a school to teach administrators the Confucian classics, reforms with an enduring effect on imperial China.

Emperor of the [[Tang dynasty]] (r. 712–756). Personal name Li Longji. His 44-year reign was the longest of the Tang dynasty. He seized the throne through two palace coups and inherited an empire in its golden age. Born in [[Luoyang]], he lived as a prince under the control of Empress Dowager Wu. Over-trusting chancellors Li Linfu and Yang Guozhong and the general An Lushan led to sharp decline, and the golden age ended in the An Lushan rebellion.

Tallest and heaviest living penguin species, endemic to [[Antarctica]]. Both sexes reach 100 cm (39 in) and feed mainly on fish, with crustaceans such as [[Krill|krill]] and cephalopods such as [[Squid|squid]]. It is the only penguin that breeds during the Antarctic winter, trekking 50–120 km (31–75 mi) over the ice to colonies. The male incubates the single egg for just over two months. Wild lifespan is typically 20 years.

Chronic [[Lung|lung]] condition marked by enlarged air spaces (alveoli) caused by breakdown of their walls. This reduces the surface available for gas exchange, lowering oxygen supply to the blood. Emphysema usually affects [[Middle age|middle-aged]] or older people, as it develops over time with the effects of [[Tobacco smoking|tobacco smoking]] and other risk factors. When it causes significant airflow limitation, it is a major subtype of [[Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease|chronic obstructive pulmonary disease]] (COPD).

[[Art Deco]] office skyscraper in Manhattan, New York City. Designed by Shreve, Lamb & Harmon, the 102-story building was constructed between 1930 and 1931 and was the world's tallest until the North Tower of the [[World Trade Center (1973–2001)|World Trade Center]] was topped out in 1970. After the [[September 11 attacks]] it was again New York City's tallest until 2012. Its owners did not make a profit until the early 1950s, because of the [[Great Depression]] and [[World War II]]. Around four million tourists visit its observatories each year, and it has appeared in more than 250 television series and films since *King Kong* (1933). Its roof height is 1,250 feet (380 m), or 1,454 feet (443.2 m) with its antenna.
